title: Atlas Reasoning Engine: Autonomous Planning vs Hardcoded Decision Trees

steps.prompt: How does the Agentforce Atlas Reasoning Engine differ from traditional chatbot rule-based decision trees when handling multi-intent customer service conversations?

options.label: Atlas evaluates context iteratively, generating dynamic plans, selecting tools, and adapting to intermediate results
options.rationale: Atlas dynamically evaluates context, generates iterative plans, orchestrates topics, selects tools, and refines execution based on intermediate observation steps.

options.label: Atlas traverses precompiled state machines where intent scores route conversations through static dialogue trees
options.distractorAntipattern: Atlas is an autonomous generative reasoning engine, not a precompiled static dialogue state machine.
options.rationale: Traditional chatbots rely on predefined dialogue trees and rigid branch logic, whereas Atlas reasons autonomously without hardcoded decision branches.

options.label: Atlas executes semantic similarity search against indexed knowledge articles and outputs top-ranked answers directly
options.distractorAntipattern: Atlas orchestrates multi-step agentic plans and tools, rather than simply returning top vector search snippets.
options.rationale: Direct semantic retrieval only answers static questions; it cannot orchestrate business actions, call APIs, or execute multi-turn transactional plans.
